# third_party/ — the dependency graph

`Cargo.lock` is what ships, not what compiles. Read this before changing a feature set or re-resolving the lock.

- **An optional dependency enters `Cargo.lock` as soon as an enabled feature references it — even weakly (`dep?/feat`).** sqlx's `migrate`/`json`/`chrono`/`uuid` features each reference `sqlx-sqlite?/…`, so the SQLite driver landed in the lock with `libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1 (RUSTSEC-2026-0459) while never being compiled: `cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys` was empty before the fix, only the lock entry was vulnerable. `cargo audit` reads the lock, so it flags crates this project never builds.
- **`third_party/sqlx-sqlite-noop` stands in for that driver** — a no-op crate named `sqlx-sqlite`, patched in via `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml` and declared as a workspace member, so the final `cargo build --release --locked` resolves it. (cargo-chef masks member versions to `0.0.1`, so the `cook` layer cannot use the stub and re-resolves the real driver there — downloaded, never compiled; the shipped binary uses the real lock.) Bump its version in lockstep with sqlx: a version that no longer satisfies sqlx's requirement makes cargo warn `patch not used`, the real driver returns to the lock, and the advisory returns with it. The root manifest pins `sqlx = "=0.9.1"` exactly for that reason — `cargo update` cannot move sqlx off the version the stub satisfies, so the two are bumped together in one commit, never apart.
- **The repo is a two-crate workspace** — the root package plus that stub — but the stub is a workspace member, **not** a default member. With a root package present and no `default-members`, Cargo's default members are the root package alone (Cargo Book, §"The default-members field": "When unspecified, the root package will be used"), so a plain `cargo build` from the root never compiles the stub. Only a workspace-wide package selection (`cargo build --workspace`, or its `--all` alias) builds it, and no gate passes either — `bin/lint`, `bin/ci` and `ci.yml` all run root-package-only commands (`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo test --all-targets --all-features`; `--all-targets`/`--all-features` select targets and features, not workspace members). `bin/lint`'s `cargo fmt --all` formats the stub but never compiles it. The stub's whole job is to exist in the lock, where the final `cargo build --release --locked` reads it.
- **Re-resolve narrowly.** Edit the manifests, run a plain `cargo metadata`, then pin stragglers with `cargo update -p <crate> --precise <v>`. `cargo update -p sqlx` alone drags sibling crates to latest (mongodb went to 3.10.2 and `mongodb-internal-macros` stayed there after mongodb was pinned back).
- **sqlx 0.9.0 is unusable here** (custom-type OID lookup clobbers the unnamed statement → SQLSTATE 26000); 0.9.1 is the floor. sqlx-sqlite 0.9.1 accepts a fixed `libsqlite3-sys`, so the stub now keeps a never-built C-library crate out of the lock rather than dodging an unresolvable advisory.
- **`pg_query` needs libclang to build.** Its build script compiles libpg_query (Postgres's parser, statically linked — the runtime image gains no library) and runs bindgen, which loads libclang: the Dockerfile's builder stage installs `libclang-dev`, and a dev box or CI runner needs clang (GitHub's Ubuntu runners ship it). Its build-only graph (`bindgen`, `prost-build`, `clang-sys`, `thiserror` 1, `itertools` 0.10) sits in the lock and in `cargo audit`'s scope. It is pinned exactly: the gateway reads the parse tree's wire bytes through two C symbols it declares itself (`src/exec/sql_guard/pg_tree/ffi.rs`, the crate's one `unsafe` module), by a schema generated from that release. Bumping it means checking those declarations against the new `pg_query.h`, running `bin/regen-pg-tree`, and the guard's tests green — a grammar change can turn an admitted spelling into a disagreement, and a new node type is refused until listed. Its build script rewrites its own `src/protobuf.rs` in the cargo registry when `protoc` is on `PATH`; keep `protoc` out of builders.
